exhibits.title: The Row of Quarrelling Portraits
exhibits.text:
Behold a row of enchanted portraits, T of them hung side by side, and understand that they are not T pictures but ONE moving picture cut into slices of an instant. Read left to right and a second of enchanted life should pass — a raised hand, a turned head, a candle-flame leaning in the draught.

Now watch what happens when each portrait is painted by its own painter, working alone, forbidden to glance at its neighbours. This is the naive spell: take the image-diffusion you mastered below, and simply run it independently, once per frame. Each painter draws a plausible instant. But painter five never saw painter four's canvas — so between the frames the cloak shifts from grey to blue and back, the candle-flame jumps to the wrong hand, the background stones rearrange themselves, the very face subtly morphs. Every single frame is, on its own, a fine picture. The SEQUENCE is a fevered flicker. This failure has a name — a want of TEMPORAL CONSISTENCY — and curing it is the whole reason this Gallery exists.

Step to the second row, where the same T portraits are painted TOGETHER, by one hand that sees every canvas at once and denoises them JOINTLY. Now the cloak keeps its colour, the flame stays on its wick, the stones hold still; the frames agree, and the picture truly moves. That is the single new law of video diffusion: denoise all T frames jointly so they remain consistent through time.

And mark well what did NOT change to achieve it. The mathematics you carried up the stair is untouched. The forward noising is the very same equation, x_t = sqrt(a_bar_t) * x_0 + sqrt(1 - a_bar_t) * eps, now applied element-wise across a whole VIDEO tensor. The reverse denoising, the ε-prediction squared loss, the latent compression through a VAE, classifier-free guidance, the U-Net or DiT denoiser at the heart — all inherited, all unaltered. Only two things are new, and the second waits in the next chamber. The first is simply the SHAPE of the canvas: it has grown a new axis, T, for time. That extra T dimension is the whole story.

exhibits.title: The Flicker — A Want of Temporal Consistency
exhibits.text:
The naive recipe for a moving picture is seductive: you already own a spell that denoises one image, so denoise each of the T frames independently and stack them. It fails, and it fails in a single, instructive way.

Each frame is drawn from its own noise with no knowledge of the others. Frame 5 has no idea what frame 4 looked like. So although every frame is individually plausible, the sequence is incoherent: colours drift between frames, objects jitter and morph, edges crawl, backgrounds shift and reshuffle. The eye reads this instantly as FLICKER. The defect is not in any one frame but in the RELATIONSHIP between frames — the property we call TEMPORAL CONSISTENCY, that a thing which is red and here in this frame stays red and here in the next.

Independence is precisely the disease. The cure is therefore not a better single-frame painter but a painter who denoises ALL frames JOINTLY — one process that sees the whole stack at once, so each frame is constrained by its neighbours. Every distinctive machine of video diffusion — first among them temporal attention, in the next chamber — is only an apparatus for enforcing that joint constraint.

exhibits.title: What You Need Not Relearn
exhibits.text:
Before cataloguing what is new, fix firmly what is NOT — for the honest surprise of this floor is how little changes. The entire diffusion framework you mastered below is inherited, unaltered, into video:

— FORWARD NOISING: the identical equation, x_t = sqrt(a_bar_t) * x_0 + sqrt(1 - a_bar_t) * eps, now run element-wise over a video tensor instead of an image tensor. Same algebra; larger array.

— REVERSE DENOISING: the same iterative walk from pure noise back to a clean sample, one step at a time.

— THE OBJECTIVE: still ε-prediction under a mean-squared-error loss, ||eps - net(x_t, t)||^2. The corruption still hands you its own answer key.

— LATENT DIFFUSION: still done in the compressed latent space of a VAE, never on raw pixels, for the same reason as ever — cost.

— CLASSIFIER-FREE GUIDANCE: the same trick steers the sample toward the prompt.

— THE DENOISER: still a U-Net or a DiT, the very architectures from the Diffusion wing.

Not one of these is rederived for video. If you understood image diffusion, you already hold nine-tenths of video diffusion. What remains is a change of SHAPE and a single new gaze along time.

exhibits.title: The One New Axis — T for Time
exhibits.text:
Hold an image in your mind as a tensor of shape (H, W, C) — height, width, channels. In latent diffusion the VAE first compresses it to a smaller latent of shape (h, w, c), and all the diffusion machinery acts on that latent. None of this is new.

A video is nothing but a STACK of T such frames. So its tensor gains one axis at the front: (T, H, W, C). Compress each frame with the same VAE and the latent becomes (T, h, w, c). That prepended T — the time axis, the number of frames — is the ENTIRE structural difference between an image and a video as far as the mathematics is concerned. The forward equation still runs element-wise; it simply now runs over an array with a T in its shape. eps is a full standard-normal draw of shape (T, h, w, c); a_bar_t remains a single scalar noise level shared across every frame and pixel.

So the data does not become a different KIND of thing. It becomes the same thing with one more index. Everything else this Gallery teaches — first and foremost the temporal attention of the next chamber — is the answer to a single question: now that the tensor has a T axis, how do we make the model reason ALONG it, so the frames stay consistent? That extra T dimension is the whole story.

exhibits.title: Image Tensor vs Video Tensor
exhibits.spec:
graph TD
  IMG["IMAGE  (H, W, C)"] -->|VAE encode| ILAT["image latent  (h, w, c)"]
  F1["frame 1"] --> STACK["stack along new axis T"]
  F2["frame 2"] --> STACK
  FT["frame T"] --> STACK
  STACK --> VID["VIDEO  (T, H, W, C)"]
  VID -->|same VAE, per frame| VLAT["video latent  (T, h, w, c)"]
  VLAT --> JOINT["denoise ALL T frames JOINTLY"]
exhibits.caption: An image is (H, W, C); a video is the same thing with one prepended axis, T, the frame count — (T, H, W, C), compressed by the same VAE to (T, h, w, c). The only new structure is that T axis. The single new demand is that all T frames be denoised JOINTLY rather than independently, so they stay consistent through time.

exhibits.title: Flicker vs Consistency, and the One New Axis
exhibits.caption: Read the two rows of panel (a) as the same second of enchanted life, painted twice. Below, each of the six frames is denoised INDEPENDENTLY, by a painter forbidden to glance at the others: the subject jitters in place and its colour lurches from blue to gold to green to violet — every frame plausible alone, the sequence a fevered FLICKER. Above, the same six frames are denoised JOINTLY, by one hand that sees the whole stack at once: the subject holds its colour and glides along a single intended path — temporally consistent. That is video diffusion's one new law. Panel (b) shows why it costs so little to obey. An image is a tensor of shape (H, W, C); a video is that very same object with one prepended index — (T, H, W, C) — a stack of frames along a new time axis T. Nothing else is re-derived: the forward noising equation, the ε-prediction loss, the VAE latents, classifier-free guidance and the U-Net/DiT denoiser are all inherited unchanged from the floor below. The whole story of this Gallery is that extra T axis, and the single demand that the model now reason along it.
